subject: Private deployment: pin window coordination and network rollback play
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmecloud.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jana Ruiz <jana.ruiz@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment — request to schedule patch window and pin

Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to schedule the maintenance window to apply the recommended security patches and the minor runtime update you proposed for our private VPC deployment. Attached is a brief request that lists two possible windows (Sept 20–21 UTC and Sept 27–28 UTC) and our preferred rollback contact list.

Key asks from our side: 
- Can Redwood pin our control-plane components to the current validated runtime until after the update window begins?
- We need a clear network rollback play if the KV cache sync times out (our ops lead will need the exact BGP/route steps).
- Please confirm any expected client-side connection rehandshake behavior (session drops, token refresh requirements).

If you can send a short runbook snippet we can review with our NetOps team, that would speed approvals.

Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Cloud Ops, AcmeCloud
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request to schedule patch window and pin

Sam — thanks for the request and the two window options. High-level responses below, and I’ve attached our preflight checklist for your NetOps team to validate.

Answers:
1) Pinning: Yes — we can pin the control-plane image/agent for your fleet until the maintenance window kickoff. That prevents automatic version roll when the runtime update lands. We’ll coordinate the unpin command at T+10 minutes after validated health checks unless you instruct otherwise.

2) Network rollback play: We’ll provide explicit route rollback commands and an ordered play of actions (drain, BGP withdraw, route re-add). NetOps will need the ephemeral route IDs which we’ll share under the secure link.

3) Client behavior: Our SDKs will attempt transparent reconnects; sessions using long-lived tokens may see a short 5–15s spike in errors during KV warmup. We recommend a short client-side retry backoff (3s, 6s, 12s) for the first 60s.

Proposed next step: quick alignment call with your NetOps and our infra lead (Vivek) tomorrow 0900 PT to walk the runbook and confirm the final window. If that works, I’ll schedule and include a run-of-show.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Technical Account Manager — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_preflight-checklist.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request to schedule patch window and pin

Adding technical notes for the call and proposing the rollback ladder we'll present: 

Preflight gating (T-72 to T-1):
- Verify KV health baseline and prefix cache hitrate >= 98% (T-72 dry run metric check)
- Confirm NetOps firewall rules permit control-plane flights and port 9000 drain traffic (T-48)
- Snapshot routing table and export BGP peers via NetOps session (T-24)

Rollback ladder (ordered):
1) Abort: cancel the rollout and re-pin — immediate if > 10% error rate sustained for 5 minutes post-kickoff.
2) Evacuate: drain traffic from canary nodes, move traffic to fallbacks (regional pool).
3) Network rollback: execute BGP withdraw of update prefixes (NetOps maintains the withdraw script — we’ll coordinate IDs).
4) Redeploy previous runtime build to the pinned group and re-warm KV from snapshot.

Edge cases: intermittent route flaps may require manual session garbage collection on client side. We'll provide a small script for NetOps to force-close stale sessions.

Vivek, can you confirm we have the prebuilt rollback image and an estimate for KV rewarm (expected 4–8 minutes per shard)?

-Neha
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request to schedule patch window and pin

Confirming: 
- Rollback image: yes, we have a validated rollback image built from the currently pinned hash (sha256: 7a3f9b...).
- KV rewarm: plan for parallel rewarm across 6 shards, ~5 minutes per shard median; worst case 12 minutes for the largest shard. We’ll include KV warmup checks in the gating policy.
- Network play: we'll provide the BGP withdraw/reannounce script as vpc-routing-diff.patch (attached) and a NetOps checklist with the exact route-ids.

Connor — please lock the canary group to the pinned image and schedule the T-0 handover. On the call we should record exactly who has the authority to abort (we recommend: AcmeCloud NetOps lead, Redwood infra lead (Vivek), and Connor as TAM).

-Vivek
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmecloud.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jana Ruiz <jana.ruiz@acmecloud.com>, NetOps Inc. <support@netops-inc.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — request to schedule patch window and pin

Connor/Team — thanks for the quick follow-up and the checklist. Sept 27–28 UTC works best for us after we sync with our NetOps partner. We confirmed a 0900 PT alignment call on Sept 15; invite accepted.

A couple items for the run-of-show: 
- Please include the exact command strings for the route withdraw and reannounce (we need these in our change ticket).
- We'll require the DocuSign change authorization link for our CAB (I’ll attach the ticket number once created).

Attaching the maintenance request PDF you requested. We'll expect the runbook link and the routing patch ahead of the Sept 15 call.

Sam
